sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole post-merge sequence
sections.what: Runs the install and data-loading steps in order after a merge. Schema changes are excluded on purpose.
sections.why: Keeps routine data synchronization automatic while leaving schema changes as a deliberate action.
sections.watch_out: The header warns that running the drizzle push command here would drop the compass tables and their data. Do not add it.

summary: Runs after a code merge to prepare the local setup: it installs packages, loads committed demo evidence and approved research, and queues report refreshes. It never changes the database schema.
purpose: Brings the code and the database back in line after a merge.
why: The header explains that schema changes must be applied on purpose, and that database rows do not come with the code, so they ship as fixtures and load safely.
how: Installs packages from the lock file. Loads the committed demo evidence fixture, which fails the step if a pinned demo is still missing examples. Replays approved research batches within a 120 second budget, and records any failure. Refreshes the value layer, where failure is tolerated. Queues report catch-up runs, where failure is also tolerated. Ends with the replay's status as its exit status.
inputs: The project files and the lock file, the replay ledger under data/yard-research, committed fixtures, and the database connection from the environment.
outputs: Installed packages, loaded database rows, queued report runs, and messages for any failures. The exit status comes from the replay step.
risks: It writes to the live database after every merge. The steps are meant to insert data only, but a bad fixture or ledger would still change data. Because the script sets fail-fast, an error in the first install or the demo fixture stops the rest.
debug: If merge setup fails, read the last message printed. A refused replay batch names the batch, so compare its digest against the ledger. For a value-layer failure, run the command the message gives by hand. To check research report status, run the catch-up command with no flags.
